one_liner: Pure-Rust SCSS/Sass compiler matching dart-sass 1.104.1 output; ships native CLI, crate, C ABI and npm (wasm plus N-API) builds.
what_it_does: Compiles SCSS and indented .sass to CSS, aiming for byte-identical output to current dart-sass (99.0% of attempted sass-spec cases, 14,114 of 14,258; 137 of 138 Lichess entry points byte-identical). It is a Rust crate (compile / compile_with_source_map with a pluggable Importer), a CLI that accepts dart-sass's arguments, a C ABI, and an npm package that mirrors the dart-sass modern JS API (compileString etc.) so it can replace `sass` in sass-loader or Vite.
how_it_is_fast: Native code with no VM or Node start-up (1.8 ms process floor against 139 ms for the dart-sass JS bin). The binary installs a scoped bump-arena global allocator (ScopedAlloc) that turns each compile's allocations into pointer bumps freed at the end, and composite values are reference-counted so passing a list or map is an O(1) refcount bump; later rounds cut allocations on the large corpus from 377,761 to 155,656. Multi-file builds compile in parallel, one worker per core by default.
when_to_use: CI or build scripts that shell out to `sass` once per file, where dart-sass's 140-500 ms start-up per invocation dominates
Embedding a Sass compiler in a Rust, Go (wazero, no cgo), Ruby, Python or PHP process without a Node or Dart toolchain
Browser or edge use where shipping the dart-sass compiler as JavaScript is too heavy (size wasm build about 356 KB gzip)
Large multi-entry trees (Lichess-style, 100+ entry points) on a multi-core machine, where its parallel CLI beats the sequential npm `sass` CLI
Projects that want current dart-sass semantics (CSS Color 4, modern serialization) that grass, pinned to dart-sass 1.54.3, does not give
when_not_to_use: Single-entry builds through the npm CLI: one Linux entry point took 38.3 ms via node_modules/.bin/sasso against 20.7 ms for dart-sass (issue #272); use the binary (4.3 ms) instead
Stylesheets relying on dart-sass 1.105 features (first-class modules, meta.load / meta.get-module, issue #281) or on --pkg-importer and deprecation-selection flags, which the binary does not support
Pipelines that need dart-sass's exact error behaviour everywhere: 62 open issues, many parity bugs (e.g. #297 and #253 compile input dart rejects, #282 @extend across media queries)
Memory-constrained parallel builds: the arena keeps each thread's high-water mark, 478 MB peak for the binary at -j 12 on Lichess and about 1.35 GB for a --watch pool
Teams that need a mature, widely deployed compiler: v0.x, 7 GitHub stars, about 2,000 crates.io downloads

integration.form: crate + CLI binary (cargo-dist, Homebrew, Nix) + npm package (wasm build plus optional N-API addon) + C ABI static/shared lib
integration.dependencies: none at runtime; chrono only on Windows for the CLI's --watch timestamp (optional cli-clock feature)
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.74 (declared rust-version); Node version for the npm package not documented beyond the Node 22 used for wasm timings
integration.platforms: any std target incl. wasm32-unknown-unknown and wasm32-wasip1; prebuilt binaries for Linux gnu/musl, macOS and Windows on x86_64/aarch64; native npm addon only on macOS and Linux (wasm fallback elsewhere)
integration.thread_safety: compile runs in a per-thread arena scope; tests/arena_threads.rs runs 8 threads x 200 concurrent compiles with byte-identical results. Send/Sync bounds of Options and Importer not checked.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — the CLI takes dart-sass's flags and the npm package mirrors the modern JS API (sass-loader, Vite alias), but legacy-API callers, --pkg-importer, deprecation-selection flags and dart-sass 1.105 first-class modules are not covered

gotchas: Harness flaw in the headline 138-stylesheet table: sasso compiles in parallel (12 threads on the 12-core M2 Max named in issue #83) while the dart-sass row does not name its form; the npm `sass` CLI compiles multiple files sequentially (dart-sass lib/src/executable/concurrent/js.dart aliases the concurrent call to the plain one; only the Dart VM build uses isolates). Single-threaded, the binary at -j 1 took 681 ms against 2322 ms (3.4x, issue #83), the npm native engine at -j 1 0.86 s against 2268 ms (2.6x, 0.16.0 changelog), and the sequential wasm CLI before 0.15.0 took 2340 ms, at parity with dart-sass; the record's ~3.7x wasm figure comes from the worker pool.

The arena speed-up is only active when ScopedAlloc is the #[global_allocator]: the CLI installs it, a Rust embedder must do so itself (the N-API addon was 14-26% slower until 0.16.0 for this reason), and the wasm builds run without it.

Harness flaw in the README's 'pure compile' row: sasso's 7.4 ms is a warm 200-iteration in-process loop, while dart-sass's ~216 ms is derived as cold single-file minus start-up, i.e. one compile on an unwarmed V8 JIT. The repo's own warm measurements of dart2js put it at 105.4 ms per compile (K=20 copies in one invocation, bench/dart_vs_grass.md) and 97.1 ms (sass JS library in-process, three_way.md), so the warm pure-compute gap is about 9-14x (9.3x within the single three_way.md run, 97.1 vs 10.4 ms), not ~29x (derived from page data). run_bench.sh also differs per engine in small ways: sasso uses --no-css while dart-sass writes to /dev/null, grass writes no files in the batch row, and grass --loop re-reads the file each iteration while sasso reads it once.

Published numbers are stale relative to the code: bench/README.md says the 7.4 ms/compile in three_way.md is from master dc5099b and the 2026-09-15 audit found a 7.4 to 10.4 ms regression; the dart-sass baseline in three_way.md and real_world.md is 1.100.0/1.101.0 and parity there was checked after whitespace and colour canonicalization, not byte-for-byte.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No sibling compiles Sass; the nearest catalogued pattern is a JS tool rewritten in a compiled language and shipped as wasm (svgo.mbt for SVG optimisation, calaminejs for spreadsheet reading). Pick sasso when the job is SCSS compilation and you can run its native binary or addon; its wasm build alone is roughly 1.5-3.5x slower than native.
verified_claims_summary: On an arm64 macOS 12-core machine (M2 Max per issue #83), the native binary compiled a generated ~26k-line stylesheet in 11.7 ms cold against 354 ms for the dart-sass 1.101.0 JS CLI and 26.5 ms for grass 0.13.4 (hyperfine); warm per-compile cost in the older full three_way.md run is 9.8-10.4 ms against 97.1 ms for the dart2js sass library in-process (about 9.3x), 63.8 ms for the sass-embedded native-VM daemon (about 6x) and 21.9 ms for grass (the README's later 7.4 ms is from a different run). On 21 real-world projects (sasso 0.7.0 vs dart-sass 1.101.0 JS CLI) end-to-end speedups were 3.5-42x, about 2.5-5.5x on the largest trees once dart-sass's 137 ms start-up is removed (derived from page data); the 138-file Lichess table (137 ms vs 2268 ms) compares a 12-thread sasso with a dart-sass form the README does not name.
status_note: Very active (0.21.0 on 2026-10-03, commits to 2026-10-07, about 1,557 commits since June 2026) and MIT OR Apache-2.0, but v0.x with 62 open issues and a tiny user base; the native binary is the form whose speed claims hold up.
